<p>I wanted a quick reference for common child and youth age-group totals, so I summarized the UN World Population Prospects (WPP) 2024 revision, using 2025 as the reference year. Figures for 2024 onward use the medium projection variant.</p>
<p><strong>World population:</strong> In 2025, the world population is projected at 8.2 billion (8,232 million). It is projected to peak in 2084 at 10.3 billion.</p>
<p><strong>Children under age 5:</strong> The number of children under 5 is 644 million in 2025. This figure peaked in 2017 at 698 million and is projected to decline to 550 million by 2100.</p>
<p><strong>Children aged 0-14:</strong> The population aged 0-14 peaked in 2020 and stands at 2.0 billion (2,008 million) in 2025.</p>
<p><strong>Children and adolescents under age 18:</strong> The population aged 0-17 peaked in 2022 and stands at 2.4 billion (2,409 million) in 2025.</p>
<p><strong>Children and adolescents under age 20:</strong> The population aged 0-19 is 2.7 billion (2,667 million) in 2025, just below its peak in 2024.</p>
<p><strong>Population under age 25:</strong> The population aged 0-24 is 3.3 billion (3,291 million) in 2025. It is projected to increase slightly and peak in 2030.</p>
